keyVerseText: And he said, Behold now, my lords, turn in, I pray you, into your servant's house, and tarry all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways. And they said, Nay; but we will abide in the street all night.
rootMeaning: The root of שָׁכַם (shâkam) is connected to שְׁכֶם (shᵉkem), meaning 'shoulder' or 'back,' which figuratively refers to the place of bearing burdens. Literally, שָׁכַם conveys the idea of inclining one's shoulder to carry a load, symbolizing the act of starting early in the day by preparing to bear the day's journey. This etymology enriches the common English gloss of 'rise early' by emphasizing the readiness and deliberate effort involved in beginning a task or journey at dawn.
usageInScripture: Across its 65 occurrences, שָׁכַם consistently conveys the notion of rising or starting early, as reflected in translations like 'rose up early' (9 times) and 'rose early' (6 times). The word appears in various contexts, including standing, going, and encamping, always highlighting the initiative and discipline of early rising. This range confirms that the term is not merely about waking up but about purposeful action initiated at the start of the day.
theologicalSignificance: The original meaning of שָׁכַם underscores a biblical principle of diligence and readiness, reflecting a heart prepared to serve and obey God promptly. Rising early to bear one's burden is emblematic of spiritual vigilance and faithful stewardship of the time God grants. For the Christian faith, this word invites believers to embrace disciplined devotion and active participation in God's work, mirroring Christ's example of purposeful action. It reminds us that faith is not passive but involves rising early to meet the Lord's call with commitment and perseverance.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 19:2, the phrase 'ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways' uses שָׁכַם to emphasize an intentional and timely departure. The word here conveys more than just waking up; it signals readiness to act according to God's direction without delay. This highlights the virtue of obedience and preparedness, encouraging believers to respond promptly to God's guidance in their daily lives.
